page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-2xCPU-4GB is a virtual server instance built on the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an AMD EPYC 7542 processor. The configuration includes 2 vCPUs with shared CPU allocation running at a clock speed of 2.0 GHz, alongside 4.0 GB of system memory, yielding 2.0 GB of RAM per core. This instance does not include bundled local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and it comes with one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark evaluations indicate entry-level performance characteristics. The shared CPU model results in poor multi-core and single-core stress-ng metrics, placing it in the bottom 10% of tested servers. Memory performance is similarly constrained, with uncached read and write large-block bandwidth scoring in the bottom 10%, and a Passmark memory score also in the bottom 10%. However, the server demonstrates moderate capability in specific single-threaded tasks, achieving average scores in Geekbench single-core execution, bzip3 single-threaded decompression, and text processing.

From a resource density perspective, this instance offers a budget-friendly option for workloads that do not require sustained high-performance CPU or memory throughput. The primary tradeoff is the shared CPU allocation, which can introduce resource contention and limits performance consistency under heavy multi-threaded loads. Given these parameters, the server is best suited for lightweight applications, basic web serving, development environments, and simple background utility tasks.
